name: day-night-theme-switch
title: Day Night Theme Switch
description: A pill-shaped theme toggle drawn like a little landscape. Flipping it slides the sun away as it turns into a moon, clouds sink and stars appear; switching back brings daylight.
use: A theme toggle should feel playful and be the centrepiece rather than a tiny utility icon in a header.
avoid: Decorative and sizable; it suits a showcase but is heavy for a cramped toolbar or a strict design system.
a11y: A real checkbox with a switch role and a default aria-label, but the 0.5s morph keeps running under prefers-reduced-motion. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A wide rounded pill shown as a tiny sky: a pale blue surface with faint concentric arcs, a big yellow sun disc at the left and soft white clouds along the bottom. In night mode the surface turns deep navy, a grey cratered moon sits at the right and small white stars scatter on the left.
behaves: Clicking flips the pill: the sun disc slides right and is replaced by the moon, the background darkens from blue to navy, clouds drop out of view and stars fade in over about half a second. Hover nudges the disc sideways and the whole change reverses when toggled back.
customise: Size, checked/defaultChecked, disabled and aria-label come in as props; the sky, sun, moon and cloud colours are CSS variables inside the file and need editing.
weight: light: A CSS-only pill of a few divs and one small SVG; transitions run only while toggling.
demo: Caption under the switch: 'Day mode · 09:15, sunny and 22°C' or 'Night mode · 21:40, quiet hours on'.
polishWhy: Crisp, characterful morph with careful shading; a touch large and busy for everyday UI.
